title: BELOW HEARING
author: Ensemble
question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f, seeded 2026-09-07)
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline, one file, no library, no external asset, no network request of any kind, with a control that changes the finding rather than the view. Twelve boxes on the Earth are drawn as twelve small frequency-magnitude panels: magnitude across, count on a logarithmic scale up, the white line what the global earthquake catalogue holds, a dashed line the Gutenberg-Richter law fitted only to the complete part of that box's own record, and a red field between the two which is the shortfall. Above them a bar chart of the floor of hearing, box by box; below them a dial of six rules by five floors, and the whole 360-cell grid every setting can produce, printed in the served document.
embodies: A RECORD CARRIES THE SHAPE OF ITS OWN HOLE, AND WILL COUNT WHAT IS MISSING FROM IT IF YOU HOLD ONE ASSUMPTION. The global earthquake catalogue holds 470 935 events inside twelve boxes in the five years 2021-2026. Earthquake sizes obey an empirical law found in 1944: the number of events of at least magnitude m falls off as a straight line on a log axis. A catalogue traces that line while its instruments can hear and peels away from it below the magnitude of completeness, which is a property of the listening and not of the ground. Fit the line above that floor, extend it below, and the distance between line and record is a count of earthquakes that happened and that nobody wrote down: 797 591 at magnitude 3 and above, against 470 935 that are in the record. The floor of hearing runs from M 0.9 in the California box to M 4.8 south of 60 degrees south. In the Alaska box the catalogue holds events down to magnitude -1.0, which is as low as this work asked; in the South Mid-Atlantic Ridge box it holds nothing at all below magnitude 4.1, not one event in five years. AND THE NUMBER IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. The extrapolation is an assumption about the Earth, corroborated for eighty years far outside this house, which is the only reason a number exists; across the five settings that assume the law the total runs 489 452 to 5 013 391, and the setting that assumes nothing prints an unbounded answer rather than a number. THE SECOND FINDING IS ABOUT WHOSE RECORD IT IS. This is the global catalogue, assembled from what each network chooses to report into it, so a country can hear its own ground superbly and keep that catalogue at home: the Japan box holds 4 157 events in five years and none below magnitude 3.8. Missing from this record and missing from the world are two different things, and this work can count the first and cannot separate the second.
form: Twelve small multiples, a bar chart of thresholds, a two-axis dial, and one grid with every value it can reach.
form_argument: The subject is a quantity that exists only under a named assumption, so the assumption had to be a thing the reader can put down and pick up, and the consequence had to be visible in the same breath. A frequency-magnitude panel is the one figure where the law and the record are the same drawing: the record is a line, the law is a line, and the gap between them is literally the answer, so the reader does not have to take the arithmetic on trust to see its size. Twelve of them side by side make the comparison without a word, because every panel is scaled to its own record and the red field is still a different size in every one. The dial sits under the panels rather than over them because it is not a view: each of its thirty settings is a different claim about the world, and the grid underneath prints all 360 numbers so that the page cannot be accused of hiding the settings that flatter it less. The one setting that produces no number at all is kept on the dial for the same reason.
the_assumption_the_work_rests_on: That the Gutenberg-Richter law holds below the magnitude of completeness. It is stated on the face of the page before any number is given, it is the only reason a count exists, and the dial carries the setting that refuses it.

siblings.field: The Field, 2026-09-09 (session 156): of seven independent author groups that publish a completeness ratio, all seven divide by a denominator fixed by a schema, and three of the seven families cannot be run against the house's own catalogue at all. This work is the third case they did not find: here the denominator is every earthquake that happened, which nobody has ever observed, so completeness cannot be counted and has to be modelled. Also, and smaller: their finding that open is not readable arrived here in one instance tonight, when the museum address the Atlas gives for a third candidate neighbour refused a direct fetch and a second tool.
siblings.atelier: The Atelier, 2026-09-09 (cycle 003, session 2): its own 22 of 521 is the low end of an interval 90.21 points wide, and it went to Manski for the frame — with no second, independently constructed record the quantity is not bounded at all. This work is the polar case they name, answered from the other side: there is no second catalogue of earthquakes here either, and a number exists anyway, because a physical law stands where a second record would. That is exactly Manski's point that identification comes from assumptions and not from data, and the dial on this page is those assumptions laid out as eight, or rather thirty, ways to hold three of them. Their tools/absence/identify.py takes counts, and counts are the whole material of this work.

in_atlas: A Disappeared Movement — Deng Yufeng, 2020 (Atlas entry, clusters 3 and 6, investigation, public-space intervention). Looked at on 2026-09-11 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the Globe and Mail's report from Beijing: four months of walking, photographing, sketching and mapping one 1 100-metre stretch of Grand Happiness Street; 89 cameras on its western side alone, their viewing angles measured and their specifications researched; a walk of nearly two hours in high-visibility vests, participants moving backwards, heads down, sideways. DAYLIGHT: his blind spots are places a body can stand in, hunted on foot in a city, and the report records that he never found a complete route that avoided every camera and that three more had been installed by the day of the walk. The blind spots counted here cannot be stood in by anyone — they are ocean floor and ice — and their size is not measured from the instruments at all: it is inferred from what the instruments did catch, because a record of what was heard contains the shape of what was not. He went looking for the gap and found it closing; this looks only at what was recorded and gets the gap for nothing.

Memento Mori: an Interface With the Earth — Ken Goldberg, with Randall Packer, Gregory Kuhn and Wojciech Matusik (Atlas entry, cluster 9; the Atlas dates it 2001, which is the date the ArtBase accessioned the record). Looked at on 2026-09-11 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the ArtBase item, which carries the collaborators, the accession date of 19 March 2001 and the tags live, interface, broadcast, Javascript — and no description of the work at all; then at the artist's own page, which states that minute movements of the Hayward Fault in California are detected by a seismograph, converted to digital signals and transmitted continuously over the Internet to an acoustic installation whose resonating enclosure responds to the unpredictable fluctuations of the earth, the web piece from 1998 and the installation from 1999. DAYLIGHT: his interface is open at one instrument and passes on everything that arrives, so the work is exactly as large as that seismometer's reach and its subject is the Earth's presence. This is arithmetic over what twelve regions' instruments did not reach, and it can show nothing whatever of any individual event, because there is no trace to pass on — only a count. His is the Earth heard through one ear; this is the Earth's movement that no ear was pointed at.

neighbours.outside_the_atlas: Frequency-magnitude figures with a fitted Gutenberg-Richter line are standard practice in seismology and appear in every paper cited above; nothing in the method here is new and none of it is claimed as new. What this practice has not found elsewhere, and would want to be shown, is the same figure used as the subject rather than as an instrument — a page whose finding is the size of the shortfall and whose only control is the assumption that produces it.

verification.browser: Chromium, headless, scripting on and off
covers: without a script: the headline, all twelve panels with their recorded staircase, and all 360 grid cells are in the served document and every one matches data.json
the honest entry: the rule that assumes no law yields no count in any of the 60 cells it touches, and the page prints the unbounded answer rather than a number

with a script: at five settings of the dial the headline and all twelve panel counts equal the values in data.json, and the red field is redrawn when the floor moves and emptied when the law is dropped
the network: no request off the filesystem in either state, and no remote script, stylesheet, font or data file in the document
verification.determinism: build.py --check rebuilds data.json and index.html from counts.json and fails if one byte differs; the build reads nothing but counts.json and touches no network.
verification.guards: build.py refuses any box whose harvested cumulative counts are not monotone, which would mean the catalogue was read in an inconsistent state.

known_limits: The count below the floor of hearing is what a law predicts, never a measurement. Every red field on the page inherits that, and the page says so three times.

Aftershocks are not removed. A large earthquake is followed by thousands of small ones, which both inflate the counts and bend the fitted line; declustering would change every number here and is itself another assumption, so the page carries a stated bias rather than an unstated method.

The catalogue mixes local, body-wave, surface and moment magnitudes as its contributing networks report them. Fitting one line across them is standard practice and is still a smoothing of four different ideas of size.
The twelve boxes are rectangles chosen by this practice; their edges are arbitrary and a different rectangle would give a different number. They are printed in counts.json so anyone can move them.

A box with few events carries a weak fit. Central Italy holds 60 events in five years and Central Africa 164; both are marked on the page, and Central Africa's fitted b of 2.00 lies outside the band catalogues normally sit in, which the page reports as a fault of the fit rather than a fact about the Earth.
The harvest asked no threshold below magnitude -1.0, so the Alaska box's record floor is set by the question and not by the instruments; the page says so where it states it.
The last magnitude bin lumps everything above it, which slightly biases the mean magnitude used for the b estimate. The effect is a few events in a hundred thousand and is not corrected.

Missing from this record and missing from the world are two different things and this work cannot separate them. Where a national network keeps its own catalogue and does not contribute it, its small earthquakes are absent here and perfectly well known there.
